## Fixed

- Keep a previously adjusted window above the taskbar when its application restores its native maximized height while inactive. Recheck the managed frame without requiring reactivation; preserve manual geometry and leave unmanaged inactive windows untouched.
- Apply completed window reads and queued follow-up events promptly even when another application responds slowly.
- Drain retired height-adjustment writers before shutdown finishes, including after monitoring and visible sessions have already been cleared. Preserve verified restoration and Accessibility recovery boundaries.

## Performance and resource use

- Reuse text measurements during button reordering and native table rows in combined/overflow lists. Preserve exact-window actions, keyboard behavior and cancellation of delayed file hover when a row is removed or reused.
- Reuse one application-candidate list per ownership pass and avoid a full window-list query when the on-screen result already confirms every tracked identity. Keep process, signer and failed-read safeguards.
- Read Space state in the existing background worker instead of on the UI thread, rejecting results from obsolete display or probe generations.
- Cancel obsolete Accessibility cleanup work, release retired diagnostic entries and remove unused wiring, test-only Release state and unconditional console dumps.

## Verification

Behavioral regressions cover production inventory, native list reuse, background probes, geometry validation and shutdown. The complete CI test suite, a separate constrained Swift-executor run, WindowLab replay, tooling, localization and deployment checks pass. The Apple Silicon package is built and verified in CI.

No new settings, permissions or runtime dependencies are introduced. Existing taskbar geometry and interaction remain unchanged.
